Genesys Cloud · Flow & resource manager

ArchyGUI

A browser front-end for the Archy CLI that moves flows and everything they depend on between Genesys Cloud orgs — safely, with history and a way back.

The problem

Archy moves a flow file. Real projects need much more.

With plain Archy CLIWith ArchyGUI
Architecture

A local web app wrapped around Archy and the Genesys API

  • Runs on your PCDouble-click start.bat → server hidden in background, UI at localhost:3737
  • Archy for flows, REST for the restExport/import via Archy; dependencies, data actions, tables, roles via the API
  • Customer data stays localcustomers.json, exported YAML and logs sit in data/ and logs/
  • Only two npm packagesexpress and axios — no build step
Two ways to use it

A delivery pipeline — or a bridge between independent orgs

① Pipeline inside one customer

  • Promote flows one stage at a time
  • Versions, drift and history visible on a board
  • Server-side guards: no cross-group writes, prod needs a deliberate confirmation

② Between independent orgs

  • Copy Data Table structures, Data Actions, flows, prompts, scripts, wrap-up codes, roles, OAuth clients…
  • Source and target are any two orgs you can log in to
  • Set the environments up as Import/export only (no stage, no group) — then no pipeline rules apply
The model

Customer → group → environment

  • Environment = one Genesys org seen through one OAuth clientName, stage, prefix, colour, region, division
  • Group = a pipelineCustomers can have several (e.g. per country)
  • Stage: dev → test → uat → prodYou can add custom stages; prod is always last
  • Prefix: only one unprefixed environment per org

Pipeline

What a promotion really does

Only a published version can be promoted — a draft has not been tested.
Prod needs your personal prod login and an explicit confirmation.
Nothing is written in the check phase.

Pipeline

The name carries its history — and counters can be aligned

Version stamp in the name

Set once, when the flow leaves the group’s first stage — then it travels unchanged. Common modules and bot flows never get a suffix (other flows call them by name).

Keep working in dev and publish: the name stays _v6 until the next promotion. The names alone show which stage is behind.

Align version number with the source

Counters are per org: dev v10 → test v3 — align publishes the missing number of times.

  • Switched on by default for Bring here
  • Max 25 extra publishes per flow
  • A target that is already higher cannot count down — the dialog says so
Pipeline

Look before you leap — and see what really happened

✔ Check — a dry run

Exports from the source, examines everything the flow references in the target — and writes nothing. Same logic as the real promotion, so they never disagree.

⇄ Check content

Compares a content hash — the only thing that can tell if two environments are really the same, whatever the version numbers say.

Board verdicts

● green — published, nothing suspicious
✗ published outside the pipeline
✗ N versions ahead of previous stage
⚠ N versions not promoted
⚠ only exists in a later stage
→ ⟵ Bring here fetches it, adds the prefix
? unknown — org could not be read
Pipeline

Release notes — and a way back

  • ↩ Roll back republishes the content from before the latest promotion — as a new version. Click again to go one promotion further back
  • Diff shows only real changes — trackingIds and export noise are removed
  • Add a note (e.g. ticket number) · Copy markdown / Download .md for the change request
  • Rollback in prod needs confirmation, like a promotion
# release note — example ## Betaling · UAT → PROD By: anna@kunde.dk Note: CHG-1234 Before: v1.0 After: v2.0 Diff: +4 −1 lines Cascade: republished 2 flows using common module Hilsen
History lives in the org (manifest table, last 20 releases). Genesys already keeps every published version, so a rollback exports the previous one straight from the org — promote from one PC, roll back from another.
Pipeline · teamwork

The org remembers — so the whole team sees the same board

  • Each org writes only about itselfTwo PCs can never disagree about the same cell
  • Two columns: key (base name + type) and Data (JSON with version, hash, who, releases)
  • Setup row ArchyGUI_Setup lets a new PC discover the environments — no secrets in it
  • Rebuild recreates a deleted table from what the org holds now
  • Needs architect:datatable:add — otherwise a local, non-shared file is used
Pipeline · dependencies

Modules only take effect when their users are republished

  • Found via Genesys dependency tracking — also through another module
  • Offered after promote, publish, import with publish and migrate
  • Republishes the published version, never a draft — flows with an unpublished draft are unticked
  • The board and Flow Browser flag a module that is newer than its users
If a republish fails, the dialog shows one line per flow: missing TTS voice, deleted queue/prompt/table, empty required field, locked flow — with Archy’s raw text under Details.
Security

Prod is locked behind you

  • Prod must use PKCE — with client credentials it can be read, not written
  • Changing a prod environment’s stage, auth, client or deploy rules needs a valid prod login — nobody can set it to “uat”, write, and set it back
  • Login is accepted only for the environment’s own org; the org is re-checked every time the token is used
  • Server binds to 127.0.0.1; file paths confined to data/flows/
  • Secrets are redacted in log and system log; names from orgs are HTML-escaped
  • Archy’s command line is quoted; names with a double quote are rejected
Restart within the 30 minutes? The login is remembered (~/.archy-gui/session.json) — no MFA again. Set rememberLoginMinutes to 0 to keep nothing.

Check first, import only after your decision

SectionContentsYou…
Can be migrated nowDataTables, Data Actions, common modules, bot flows, transfer targets, user prompts, scriptstick — migrated before the flow
Needs a decisionDivision (create / use Home / skip), survey form, TTS engine the target lackspick per resource
Create manuallyQueues, users, skills, wrap-up codes, schedules, knowledge bases, Function Data Actionscreate in target first
  • Migrate selected and continue, Continue anyway or Skip this flow
  • Division the flow is created in is checked before importing
  • Empty shells from a failed import (v1.0, only Disconnect) are never mistaken for existing flows
  • Everything missing is also in the System Log
Architect Scripting session ended in error ( code: 99 ) — full Archy output: C:\Tools\Archy\archyHome\debug\archy-debug-….txt

Archy’s generic error is explained: the message carries the path to its full output.

Migrate Flow · example

A flow brings what it uses — deepest dependency first

  • Common modules are migrated with the same machinery — recursively, bottom-up
  • A module using 15 tables brings all of them — plus its data actions (incl. secure), prompts and scripts
  • A survey flow brings its survey form, copied and published in the target
  • Outbound flows bring their contact lists
Cannot be checked: skills picked at runtime (FindSkill(Task.Skills)) and users/queues given as expressions — verify those yourself.
Migrate Flow · Data Actions

A flow finds a data action by category + name

  • choose = same name under another category — pick which one. not found = point it at an existing one, or migrate it in the next step
  • The reference is rewritten in a side copy that is imported — the source’s own copy is never touched
  • Choices are saved per org pair (in the manifest table, or .data-action-map.json) — after a successful import

⛔ Function Data Actions block

Their template URL is the id of a function in the source org. No API can create that function elsewhere — so the promotion is stopped.

checklist to copy ☐ create function data action Get customer ☐ in target org ☐ press Check again
This keeps the version number and the check in step, instead of fixing things afterwards directly in Genesys.

Example · independent orgs

Standing up a new customer org from a reference org

Data Tables — structure only

  • Select tables → ⚡ Migrate selected
  • Rows do not come along — only the column definition
  • Division is kept if it exists in the target, otherwise the default division is used (the log says so)
  • 💾 Download backup saves the structure as JSON without writing to any org

OAuth clients, integrations, roles

  • Genesys cannot hand out secrets — every new client gets a new secret, shown once → 💾 Download secrets
  • Role permissions with division/queue conditions are skipped and logged — roles never become stronger than in the source
  • Integration credentials (API keys, basic auth) are manual work; an OAuth client migrated in the same session is wired up automatically

Good to know

  • Log in → give yourself the migrated roles in the target → log in again → migrate the clients
  • Same name already in the target → skipped
  • Category names must match between orgs
Migrate resources

Sort out the names before migrating flows

Full check — every source data action vs the target
  • Filters: match · saved choice · to choose · missing · FDA missing
  • Use suggestions + Save mapping for the whole org pair
  • Check contracts compares input/output schemas — same name can still not fit
Setup proposal — capacity bars per integration (demo data)
  • Source has few integrations, target has many? Enter the limit per integration
  • Missing actions are proposed into active integrations of the same type that have room
  • Move a group to another integration — nothing is written until you migrate

Everyday tools

The rest of the toolbox

📋 Flow Browser

Search and filter by flow type. Publish checked-in drafts, 🔁 Users for modules, ⚠ for modules newer than their flows.

⇄ Compare two orgs

Exports from both and compares content — verdict: identical, N differences, or missing. 📌 Set baseline catches direct edits later.

🔀 Across customers

Flows that exist at more than one customer — e.g. the same module — with version, publish time, active. One API call per customer.

📤 Export YAML

One flow or the whole environment with live progress. Wildcards: DEV_*log finds DEV_Create Logitems.

📥 Import YAML

Paste, upload or drag-drop. 🔍 Validate in the browser, 🌐 Check against org verifies division, queues, tables, actions, prompts before import.

🗂 YAML Files

Every exported flow, split into name · version · type · customer. Latest only, and 🧹 Clean up old versions (keep 2 by default, you approve the list).

⚙ Org settings tab

Compares statuses, default language, supported languages, allowed domains and trusted IPs. Only statuses and default language are copied — IP/domain lists are read-only on purpose.

📦 Releases & reports

Markdown release notes for change requests; CSV migration report with Danish-Excel-friendly encoding (semicolon + BOM).

🐞 Report a bug

Prefilled GitHub draft issue with version, Node, OS and cleaned log lines — you press Submit.

Terraform tab

From an org to Terraform code — and into another org

① Full export

Genesys’ own exporter dumps every object as .tf. Pick types or take all; flows come along as YAML.

② Quick starting setup

Generates a clean starter from the source org’s objects — for the customer to terraform apply themselves.

③ Working folders

Edit resources in a form, run tasks, then Init · Fmt · Validate · Plan · Apply — without leaving the app.

Terraform · Full export

One folder per export — with or without a target

# data/terraform/<from>[_<to>]/<date>_full/ ├─ one .tf file per type ├─ architect_flows/ ← flows as YAML ├─ export_errors.json ← per missing scope └─ terraform.tfstate ← only WITHOUT a target
No targetWith target
Stateincludednone
plan0 changes until you editcreates everything
Usemanage the source itselfcopy to another org
  • Your login is reused — passed as GENESYSCLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN, also a personal PKCE login. No secret is ever written to the folder
  • Scope check first: every missing OAuth scope is listed at once, with a copy button — fix the client or export anyway
  • A type with a missing scope is left out and the export restarts (attempt 2, 3 …) — users and groups never vanish because of the voicemail scope
  • Include dependencies turns on enable_dependency_resolution
  • Provider is downloaded once to a shared plugin cache
“Creating” and “apply” in the export log refer only to the exporter’s helper resource in a local file — the org is only read.
Terraform · Working folders

Edit, plan, apply — one org per folder

Resources

Form built from the provider’s schema. Required fields marked, rest under More fields. { } switches a field to HCL. Comments survive edits.

Files

.tf, .tfvars, YAML and README in an editor. State, plans and .terraform/ are off limits.

Tasks

Create queues, groups, skills, wrap-up codes, languages: names, one per line, optionally copy settings from an existing one.

Plan & apply

Init, Fmt, Validate, Plan. Limit the plan to what you touched (-target) — header shows N changes waiting for apply.

A full export always has drift — a first plan on a real org can want to change hundreds of objects (credentials and OAuth clients the exporter only knows as placeholders). A red warning is shown and apply needs an extra yes.
# Tasks → groups names: testgruppe copy settings from: (optional) existing group # Archy writes the block, then runs: terraform plan -target genesyscloud_group.testgruppe Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. # nothing happens in the org before… terraform apply ← your click # later: remove the resource → next apply # deletes it in the org

Summary

What to remember

1

Pipeline

Customer → group → environments. Promote one stage at a time.

2

Check first

Dry run lists blockers, decisions and what is handled automatically.

3

Dependencies

Tables, actions, prompts, modules travel with the flow — bottom-up.

4

Truth = content

Hash compare, drift warnings — version numbers are per org.

5

History & rollback

Releases live in the org’s manifest table; roll back from any PC.

6

Prod is guarded

Personal PKCE login, deploy permission, explicit confirmation.

7

Any two orgs

Import/export-only environments copy tables, actions, flows, roles, clients.

8

Terraform

Export, edit in a form, plan limited to what you touched, then apply.

Questions

Quick quiz — click a card to reveal the answer

Q1

Dev is at v10, test at v3. Does that mean test is behind?

No. Version numbers are per-org counters. Use ⇄ Check content (hash) — or align the numbers on promote.

Q2

A flow uses a Function Data Action that doesn’t exist in the target. What happens?

The promotion is blocked. Create the function in the target org, then press “Check again”.

Q3

You copy a Data Table to another customer’s org. Do the rows come along?

No — only the column structure. Download backup saves the structure as JSON.

Q4

Someone edited prod directly in Architect. How do you see it — and fix it?

“Published outside the pipeline” / “N versions ahead” on the board; ⇄ Check content, then ⟵ Pull back to bring prod’s content down.

Q5

You want a one-off copy between two unrelated customers’ orgs. How do you set it up?

Create both as Import/export-only environments (no stage, no group) — no pipeline rules apply.

Q6

A common module changed. What must you remember?

The flows that use it only pick up the change when republished — 🔁 Republish users.

For discussion

Which customers should we set up as a pipeline first? · Who owns the manifest table in each org? · Do we want Terraform exports as part of every handover?
